reasons: Section 28.1 selects Singapore law with exclusive Singapore courts, which is outside the accepted set (NY/DE/CA/E&W) and in the rule's walk-away territory, so a deviation classification is correct and not an over-flag of an acceptable fallback.

The redline reaches the preferred position (New York law) and resolves the direct conflict with Section 28.2 by deferring jurisdiction and venue to that section, leaving the escalation step and injunctive-relief carve-out intact.

The failed minimal-edit heuristic (0.927 changed-character ratio) is expected here: the entire operative content of 28.1 is the jurisdiction and forum wording the rule requires replacing, so the rewrite is still the smallest edit that reaches the playbook position.

The comment is accurate, concise, in the required voice and prefix, correctly cites the playbook's accepted-law set and explains both the substitution and the removal of the internal conflict; the minor added conflict-of-laws phrase is standard and non-prejudicial.
